articles.title: Macklemore donates the million dollars from Ed Sheeran's tour after being dropped over his pro-Palestine speeches
articles.standfirst: The American rapper has challenged Robert Kraft to match the amount
articles.summary: The American rapper has challenged Robert Kraft to match the amount
articles.body:
The rapper Macklemore has announced that he will donate the one million dollars from his net earnings from the tour with Ed Sheeran to six organizations that directly support the Palestinian people . A decision that comes after intense controversy in which the artist was removed from the tour for his pro-Palestine speeches on stage.

To understand the origin of the conflict, we have to go back to his opening performances on September 4 and 5 at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, where the artist exclaimed "Free Palestine!" and displayed the Palestinian flag. This provoked the reaction of billionaire Robert Kraft (owner of the stadium and the Kraft business group), who pressured, along with other venue managers, to veto him , threatening to cancel the shows if he remained on the lineup. Under the pressure, the promoter decided to exclude him.

Macklemore's move has caused a domino effect on Ed Sheeran's tour

For his part, Ed Sheeran claimed that he preferred to remain neutral on political matters and that the final decision depends on contracts with promoters and venues. However, the rapper's expulsion has caused a domino effect on his tour. And also leaving the tour were the opening acts Finneas (musician, producer and Billie Eilish's brother), the Danish band Lukas Graham, artist Aaron Rowe and the Irish group Beoga .

Upon announcing the donation of his one million dollars, Macklemore publicly challenged Robert Kraft to match the amount on the grounds that "Palestinian lives deserve to be protected." “I will continue supporting the Palestinian people and their struggle for liberation” , he said.

Surprisingly, Kraft took up the gauntlet and announced that he will donate two million dollars to combat the humanitarian crisis in Gaza . The magnate said that this amount had already been suggested to him by Ed Sheeran himself before the public challenge to help mitigate the emergency in the region.

articles.title: The Million-Dollar She-Wolf: How Shakira built a historic fortune by monetizing her split from Piqué
articles.standfirst: The singer has grossed more than 400 million for her "Las mujeres ya no lloran World Tour"
articles.summary: The singer has grossed more than 400 million for her "Las mujeres ya no lloran World Tour"
articles.body:
In 2023, Shakira 's career was not at its best. At that time, it had been 6 years since her last full-length album, ‘El Dorado’, which was not very well received. On the Rate Your Music website, the Colombian artist's musical project had received a rating of 2.3 out of 5 . Although some songs she released did make it into the global top charts, the singer was not going through her most successful professional moment.

It was then that on January 11, 2023, Shakira released her joint session with the Argentine producer Bizarrap, ‘Shakira: Bzrp Music Session Vol. 53’ . The song about her breakup with Piqué was a huge success. It won 2 awards at the Latin Grammys: Song of the Year and Best Pop Song. But without a doubt, its greatest achievement was getting her music to become part of the popular conversation.

A residency in Madrid that will sell more than 600,000 tickets

Now, the album ‘Las mujeres ya no lloran’ by the Colombian artist is sweeping across the world . More specifically in Madrid, where the singer begins today her run of 12 concerts, for which, according to promoters’ estimates, more than 600,000 tickets will be sold.

“Her artistic hunger is infinite. Shakira is very persistent: any goal she sets for herself, she achieves” , said Luis Merino, who was the director of Los40 for many years, to El País. Some claim that the Colombian singer would not stop until she surpassed the figure of the 10 concerts held at the Metropolitano Stadium by Bad Bunny. And she has ended up achieving it.

"Las mujeres ya no lloran World Tour" has become the highest-grossing tour by a Latin artist. In total, it has grossed more than 400 million euros . Even so, there are those who criticize the artist because Madrid will be her only stop in Europe. One of them is the Colombian cultural promoter and musicologist Gustavo Chucky García, who states in El País that he does not know whether it is a residency or a business venture. “I believe Shakira’s concerts in Madrid are more about marketing than art,” he concludes.
